articles.title: Foreign investors flee South Korean stocks as AI boom loses steam
articles.summary: Investing.com -- South Korean stocks are struggling to attract buyers as enthusiasm for artificial intelligence-related investments fades, triggering heavy f...
articles.body:
Investing.com -- South Korean stocks are struggling to attract buyers as enthusiasm for artificial intelligence-related investments fades, triggering heavy foreign outflows and a sharp decline in trading activity.

Trading turnover in South Korea's $4.3 trillion equity market has plunged 70% from its late-May peak, while the benchmark Kospi has fallen 22% in the second half of 2026, according to Bloomberg.

The reversal follows a first-half rally that made the Kospi the world's best-performing major equity benchmark, driven largely by demand for AI memory chips.

Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix, which together account for more than half the index's weighting, have become a source of vulnerability as investors question whether the semiconductor boom can continue.

Foreign investors have withdrawn $131 billion from Korean equities this year, the largest outflow among major Asian markets, according to exchange data compiled by Bloomberg.

Concerns over demand were evident when Samsung shares declined Thursday despite the company reporting a nearly ninefold increase in quarterly operating profit.

Market support from corporate share repurchases is also weakening. Samsung and SK Hynix are approaching completion of combined buyback programmes worth 55 trillion won ($41 billion).

Retail participation has similarly declined following July's selloff.

Outstanding margin loans have fallen to approximately 33 trillion won from a June peak of 38.6 trillion won, while brokerage deposits have dropped to around 100 trillion won from nearly 140 trillion won.

Investors are increasingly favouring Taiwan, whose technology sector offers broader exposure to the AI supply chain.

Taiwan's Taiex has gained 70% this year, outperforming the Kospi by approximately 23 percentage points last quarter.

UBS Global Wealth Management said it prefers Taiwan equities for tactical AI exposure, citing the market's diversified technology hardware ecosystem and strong capital spending by major technology companies.

Despite the downturn, South Korea remains among 2026's stronger-performing markets overall, supported by earlier gains and expectations of continued AI infrastructure investment.

articles.title: A Western Digital (WDC) Investor’s Losses Prompt Jim Cramer to Bring Up Micron (MU)
articles.summary: During the October 7 episode of Mad Money, a caller said they had been averaging down on Western Digital Corporation (NASDAQ:WDC) but remained significantly...
articles.body:
During the October 7 episode of Mad Money, a caller said they had been averaging down on Western Digital Corporation (NASDAQ: WDC ) but remained significantly underwater. They asked whether to wait for a recovery or sell. Jim Cramer replied:

Well, okay, Western Digital's up 135% for the year. So, when you see that, you say to yourself, "Wow, I mean, like, either I missed it, or easy money's been made." But the way I look at Western Digital is: it's not as good as Micron. Micron's much cheaper. We know Micron really well here. We like it a lot. We think it could go much higher. I'm a swapper of Western Digital, which I did at one point own almost 5% of... That's when I was able to own stocks... It looks really good. But Western Digital is not as good as Micron.

Cramer's preference does not mean Western Digital lacks bullish backing. Both companies appeared in a screen of Reddit-trending stocks with substantial analyst-implied upside, although they occupied different positions in the ranking.

Two Different Ways to Benefit From Growing Data Demand

Western Digital Corporation (NASDAQ:WDC) focuses on hard disk drives following the separation of its flash business into Sandisk. Micron Technology, Inc. (NASDAQ: MU ) manufactures semiconductor memory and storage products. Both serve growing data requirements, but their products and manufacturing economics differ.

Western Digital's fiscal fourth-quarter revenue increased 44% year-over-year to $3.75 billion. Adjusted earnings reached $3.56 per share, while free cash flow was approximately $1.28 billion. Management projected fiscal first-quarter revenue growth of 42% to 49%, highlighting that the company's operating outlook remained strong despite the caller's disappointing investment experience. Western Digital's rally also placed it near the top of a three-year ranking of AI-linked stock returns . The accompanying coverage highlighted a supply imbalance that could help explain more than just rising sales.

Micron reported fiscal fourth-quarter 2024 revenue of approximately $54.23 billion, compared with $11.32 billion a year earlier, and adjusted earnings of $33.42 per share. Its customer agreements also provide greater visibility. Management reported approximately $150 billion of remaining performance obligations under agreements containing committed volumes and defined pricing arrangements. These commitments extend beyond a single quarter and should not be confused with immediate revenue. Those agreements are central to Cramer's argument that Micron deserves a different investment lens . How far they change its exposure to the memory cycle remains the more consequential question.

articles.title: Oil theft is on the rise in the heart of U.S. shale country—and it’s mostly carried out in targeted, organized heists
articles.summary: According to a Dallas Fed survey, 32% of executives who were impacted by oil theft said it had increased slightly over the last 12 months.
articles.body:
The spike in oil prices since the Iran war began this year has attracted more thieves, and they are increasingly professional criminals.

West Texas Intermediate crude is up 60% so far this year, and fuel prices have risen even more as global refining capacity has fallen due to the Mideast and Russia-Ukraine wars.

While oil theft has long been a part of the industry, the problem has become prevalent enough for the Dallas Fed to ask about in its quarterly surveys.

The latest one showed that nearly half of firms that are primarily focused in the Permian Basin said their operations have been impacted by theft in oil fields. By contrast, 86% of firms operating mostly outside the Permian said they were not impacted.

The Permian is the heart of the oil patch and the epicenter of the shale revolution that has transformed the U.S. into an energy superpower.

It stretches across the vast expanses of West Texas and southeastern New Mexico—and is dotted with drilling rigs, pipelines, trucks and other infrastructure necessities.

That's made the Permian a target-rich environment. And now that U.S. oil prices have been hovering around $100 a barrel lately, criminals can't resist the payoff.

According to the Dallas Fed survey, 32% of executives who were impacted by oil theft said it had increased slightly over the last 12 months, while 47% said it remained the same, and 22% said it decreased slightly or significantly.

Nearly half of the oil executives (47%) said the most common form of theft was targeted and organized, while 42% described it as opportunistic petty theft.

Still, the losses were relatively minimal, with 84% saying the financial impact of the theft was low.

A year ago, the Dallas Fed asked a slightly different set of questions about theft, including what exactly was stolen: 61% said crude oil; 58% said piping, valves and wiring; 39% said equipment; 27% said tools; and 12% said construction equipment and vehicles.

Theft can also be committed by other firms. In August, executives from a wastewater disposal company were charged with felony oil theft, money laundering and organized crime.

It was part of an investigation dubbed Operation Black Market Basin that resulted in the seizure of more than $12 million in petroleum products, vehicles, cash and other assets, according to the Texas Railroad Commission , which regulates the industry.

The investigation involved petroleum allegedly acquired and sold across Texas, New Mexico and Oklahoma, the commission added.

And in April, federal prosecutors announced charges in a large-scale oil theft conspiracy in the Permian Basin to transport stolen crude oil across the New Mexico-Texas border for resale.

articles.title: Green cards not key to workforce strategy: TCS CEO
articles.summary: TCS CEO says green cards aren’t central to staffing strategy, as US local hiring rises to 50%; firm adds 15,000 US jobs and grows AI revenue past $3.1B.
articles.body: Bengaluru: TCS CEO K Krithivasan said green cards have never been a key part of the company’s workforce strategy, as it has significantly reduced permanent residency applications for H-1B employees and stepped up local hiring in the US. The company said the US suspension of green card processing would not fundamentally alter its talent management approach.“In the last few years, what Sudeep (CHRO) and his team have been applying for is a single-digit kind of green card permanent residency,” Krithivasan said.TCS has been increasing local hiring in the US, where locally hired employees now account for 50% of its workforce. The company plans to hire another 15,000 people in the country over the next five years. TCS had around 11,000 H-1B employees in its 30,000-strong US workforce.TCS said its model involves employees travelling from India to work on client projects in the US for two to three years before returning. “There is a continuous movement of talent between onsite and offshore,” Krithivasan said.TCS said fresher hiring would continue to be driven by demand rather than a fixed target of 40,000. The company onboarded 10,000 freshers in the September quarter, compared with 14,000 in the preceding quarter.It has also increased its intake of AI-native talent from Indian universities by 50% as it builds capabilities for AI-led technology services. “We have increased intake by 50% because we find very good success in them being very natural. They’re building great credibility with our customers and able to deliver outstanding results,” TCS chief human resources officer Sudeep Kunnumal said.TCS added 4,258 employees during the quarter, taking its headcount to 5.9 lakh.The company’s annualised AI revenue crossed $3.1 billion, accounting for more than 10% of overall revenue. Krithivasan said TCS was seeing a new category of deals, including those with Porsche and Best Buy, in which it helps clients rethink their operating models as AI changes business requirements.“We are not looking at it as acquisition of revenue or protecting revenue. These are two new classes of deals where we help the customers transform them fully,” he said, adding that the objective was to help clients become AI-first enterprises.TCS expects AI-led opportunities to offset productivity-driven deflation in traditional technology services, though a stronger net growth contribution could take time. Krithivasan estimated a six-quarter to three-year horizon for the balance to shift more decisively.Technology spending could remain flat or see a slight increase as clients invest in AI, technology modernisation and business operations, he said. TCS’s dollar revenue rose 0.2% sequentially and 2.4% year on year to $7.6 billion in the September quarter. Constant-currency growth was 0.5% sequentially and 2.8% year on year, marking its weakest September-quarter sequential growth in three years.Krithivasan said TCS follows a disciplined approach to reporting AI revenue. “We count work involving AI for technology modernisation, operations modernisation, business outcomes, fine-tuning or testing models. If we use AI in software engineering to improve productivity, we do not count that as AI revenue,” he said.The company is also looking to reduce subcontracting expenses, which rose to support project ramp-ups. “Our focus is to bring them down because subcontracting is an important margin lever. Costs rose as we had to support certain ramp-ups, but we are comfortable returning to the levels that existed two quarters ago,” he said.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. articles.title: Oil falls on hopes Russia-Ukraine energy ceasefire will boost supplies
articles.summary: By Florence Tan SINGAPORE, Oct 12 (Reuters) - Oil prices slipped on Monday on expectations of more Russian supplies after US President Donald Trump said Ukra...
articles.body:
SINGAPORE, Oct 12 (Reuters) - Oil prices slipped on Monday on expectations of more Russian supplies after US President Donald Trump said Ukraine and Russia had agreed to halt attacks on each other's energy facilities following a ‌US diesel-supply deal with Moscow.

Brent crude futures fell $1.54, or 1.47%, to $103.18 a barrel by 0154 GMT while US West Texas ‌Intermediate crude was at $90.31 a barrel, down $1.54, or 1.68%.

ICE gasoil futures fell 3% to $1,436 per barrel after President Trump said on Friday that Russia will immediately supply more ​than 300,000 metric tons (2.25 million barrels) of diesel to US and global markets.

Russia would supply another 500,000 tons in November and a further 1 million tons "immediately thereafter", Trump added. The daily diesel consumption globally is forecast at close to 29 million barrels, according to the International Energy Agency.

Trump also unexpectedly announced on Sunday that Ukraine and Russia had agreed to an energy ceasefire, but Ukrainian leader Volodymyr Zelenskiy said he was still ‌waiting to see details of the energy ceasefire ⁠while Russia did not comment.

The announcements eased some of the immediate supply pressure, Tim Waterer, KCM Trade chief analyst, said.

"Questions remain over the validity and longevity of any such ceasefire, and without clearer evidence that it ⁠will actually hold, the extent of the pullback is likely to stay limited," he added.

IEA's Executive Director Fatih Birol said on Sunday that all members should assess whether additional diesel releases are necessary and that countries which have not yet fully delivered pledged volumes accelerate their remaining releases prioritising diesel.

CRUDE ​SUPPORTED ​BY MIDDLE EAST CONFLICT

However, the Middle East conflict continued to support Brent crude ​at above $100 a barrel.

The Houthis claimed responsibility for a ‌Saturday strike on Riyadh's international airport that killed 13 people and wounded more than 300, while Saudi authorities reported that people were injured in a new attack on the airport on Sunday.

US President Donald Trump said on Saturday the United States was considering joining Saudi strikes on the Houthis in the conflict, a spillover from the wider war with Iran that the US and Israel launched in February.

In addition, more attacks on tankers sailing through the Strait of Hormuz have been reported so far this month, threatening to dampen a recovery in ‌Middle East crude exports seen in September.

A tanker was struck by a drone in ​the vicinity of Sohar anchorage, Oman, while another was damaged by an unknown ​projectile while transiting the Strait of Hormuz, the United Kingdom ​Maritime Trade Operations reported over the weekend.

articles.title: Goyal backs global growth push for Indian startups; Gajwani flags AI gap
articles.summary: BENGALURU: Commerce and industry minister Piyush Goyal called on Indian start-ups to look beyond the domestic market and expand overseas, offering govt
articles.body: BENGALURU: Commerce and industry minister Piyush Goyal called on Indian start-ups to look beyond the domestic market and expand overseas, offering govt funding to showcase them at international exhibitions and conferences. He said a sustained three-to-five-year push could help startups tap new markets and attract investors. Goyal also argued that tighter H-1B visa access could benefit India by retaining talent and bringing more work to the country’s global capability centres.“We are willing to fund whatever it takes to take our startups to the rest of the world,” Goyal said at the ET Startup Awards 2026 in Bengaluru on Friday. “Let’s get out of the cozy comfort of the large Indian opportunity or Indian market. Let us think of going global,” he added.Times Internet chairman Satyan Gajwani flagged India’s lag in artificial intelligence, saying the country needs deeper research, greater computing power and patient capital to close the gap with the US and China.“As the US and China race ahead in artificial intelligence, India’s progress has been slower than it should be,” Gajwani said. He also added that India is witnessing a maturing startup ecosystem, with founders increasingly focused on deep, proprietary technology. Citing the launch of Skyroot Aerospace’s Vikram-1 rocket, he said the achievement signalled the growing capabilities of Indian startups in deep tech. “Indian startups are now building semiconductor chips, AI robotics, clean energy technologies and new materials while investors are shaping funds willing to wait longer for these companies to mature,” Gajwani said.He attributed this shift to entrepreneurial ambition, founders turning investors and govt support. “This maturing of the Indian startup ecosystem, this energy and this audacity, founders paying it forward as investors, the structural backing by the state — they’ve all come together thanks to a lot of advocacy and championing by many of our leaders,” he said. India has grown from a few hundred recognised startups to more than 2.5 lakh, creating close to 25 lakh jobs, Gajwani added.Moderating a panel on India’s deep tech ambitions, Accel India founding partner Prashanth Prakash said building such companies required infrastructure and regulatory changes beyond those needed for conventional software businesses. “To build deep tech we need all these enabling elements that were not required for just a software company,” he said.Agrani Labs cofounder and CEO Dheemanth Nagaraj, whose company is developing AI GPUs for data centres, said Indian products had to compete globally on quality. “There is no space for building a substandard product at a lower cost,” he said. Govt could help create a market by becoming a first customer, he added.Spacetech firm Pixxel cofounder and CTO Kshitij Khandelwal said reforms had eased satellite licensing, but setting up manufacturing facilities remained challenging. “The issues that we have faced mostly are local in nature,” he said.BrainSight AI cofounder and CEO Laina Emmanuel said mapping brain function requires complex science and significant computing power. “It’s hard science, it’s hard tech, it’s hard market building for us,” she said.At a panel on the journey to listing, Meesho CEO Vidit Aatrey recalled retired investors at the company’s first annual general meeting, telling him they were investing savings accumulated over their lifetimes. “Now you are responsible for their money, and you have to behave differently,” he said.Groww CEO Lalit Keshre said the listing strengthened the connection between the company and its users, many of whom also became shareholders. The company continued to pursue its long-term goals through regular reviews. “The philosophy is that you think long term, but you execute short term.”You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. articles.title: Share markets choppy in Asia as earnings loom, oil slips
articles.summary: By Wayne Cole SYDNEY, Oct 12 (Reuters) - Stock markets got off to an erratic start on Monday as earnings season looked set to test high tech valuations, whil...
articles.body:
SYDNEY, Oct 12 (Reuters) - Stock markets got off to an erratic start on Monday as earnings season looked set to test high tech valuations, while oil slipped amid confusion over whether Russia would, or could, increase energy exports.

While the conflict in ‌the Gulf continued with strikes on shipping and airports, President Donald Trump's announcement of an energy ceasefire between Ukraine and Russia muddied the ‌waters on oil supply.

Trump's proposal for Russia to increase its exports of diesel added to the mix, though it also drew opposition from Republican and Democratic senators as potentially illegal.

Brent futures started ​higher but soon slipped 1.3% to $103.38 a barrel, below a recent top of $109.97, while US crude futures lost 1.7% to $90.29 a barrel. [O/R]

South Korean stocks fell 3.1% and Taiwanese shares eased 0.2%. MSCI's broadest index of Asia-Pacific shares excluding Japan dipped 0.4%, while Chinese blue chips slipped 0.1%.

On Wall Street, S&P 500 futures edged up 0.3%, while Nasdaq futures gained 0.4%. In Europe, EUROSTOXX 50 futures rose 0.5%, DAX futures gained 0.6% and FTSE futures added 0.4%.

Trade was thin with Japanese markets shut ‌and the US on a partial holiday ahead of ⁠earnings season, with major US banks kicking off on Tuesday.

TSMC, the world's largest manufacturer of advanced AI chips, will likely report a sixth consecutive quarter of record earnings on Thursday.

S&P 500 earnings are expected to jump by more than 30% ⁠in the third quarter, according to LSEG IBES, though the bulk of that comes from the tech sector.

My Bui, an economist at AMP, said all the gains in the S&P 500 since mid-September had been in tech, while investors were demanding higher yields to fund the massive borrowing for AI.

The US investment-grade credit default swap index, which ​tracks ​the cost of insurance against default, had also risen sharply to its highest level since ​the US-Israeli war on Iran began.

"Overall, wider spreads suggest investors ‌are questioning whether AI revenues can keep pace with rising borrowing costs," Bui said. "Corporate bond issuance to fund AI capex, combined with wider high-yield spreads, will raise refinancing costs as the current wave of debt matures over the next few years."

The flood of corporate debt has added to pressure in sovereign markets, driving Treasury yields to 24-year highs last week while lifting the discount applied to company earnings.

The market faces fresh challenges this week from US data on consumer and producer prices and retail sales. Rising energy costs are expected to lift CPI by a hefty 0.6% ‌to an annual 3.7%, though the core is seen cooler at 0.2% and 2.5%.

articles.title: RBI measures see sharp impact as rupee rises 1% against US dollar; what steps were announced?
articles.summary: RBI has record forex reserves, but why is rupee still not out of the woods?
articles.body: RBI has record forex reserves, but why is rupee still not out of the woods?The rupee gained a stunning 1% at the start of trading on Monday after the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) eased pressure on the currency by shifting oil companies' dollar purchases away from the spot market and taking steps to curb corporate demand for forward dollars.The rupee began Monday’s session at 95.76 against the US dollar, compared with its Friday closing level of 96.73.In fact, it emerged as one of Asia's strongest-performing currencies, even as most regional currencies moved within a narrow range. Despite Monday's sharp rise, the rupee has lost 6.6% against the dollar so far this year, according to a Reuters report.Also Read | RBI has record forex reserves, but why is rupee still not out of the woods?RBI announces measures for rupeeOn Saturday, the RBI announced a set of measures targeting two major sources of pressure on the rupee. These include sustained dollar purchases by oil marketing companies amid elevated crude prices and demand from corporates looking to protect themselves against further currency depreciation.Fears of additional weakness in the rupee had prompted importers to increase their purchases of forward dollars to shield themselves from potentially higher costs in the future.However, the increased demand for hedging also put further pressure on the currency. This created a cycle in which expectations of depreciation encouraged more hedging, adding to the rupee's weakness and reinforcing those expectations.Among the measures announced by the RBI were a ban on companies rebooking cancelled rupee-linked derivatives, a reduction in the threshold for transactions that do not have an underlying exposure, and a requirement for banks to maintain a 20% cash reserve against certain foreign-exchange contracts. These steps could make hedging against a weaker rupee more expensive.Citi said in a note that the package increases the immediate cost of trades aimed at benefiting from rupee depreciation.Bankers clarified that the restrictions do not cover every foreign-exchange transaction and apply only to current account transactions.The 20% cash requirement also excludes companies hedging external commercial borrowings and foreign portfolio investors seeking to hedge their investments in India.The rupee has recovered sharply following the RBI's announcement, but analysts believe the durability of the gains will depend on whether the underlying pressures on the currency begin to ease."Beyond the initial impact, the rupee’s trajectory will continue to be shaped by crude oil prices, foreign portfolio flows and the broader direction of the US dollar," Societe Generale said in a note.You use AI every day.
